summary: The help file for the Utah-10 implementation of the user FTP process, offered as the only documentation produced so far. It covers control characters and gives a detailed command listing.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 412 reproduces the help text for the Utah-10 user FTP process. It explains the command interface and shows how users could select hosts, transfer files and choose data settings.

questions: what commands did the utah ftp process support
how did the ftp process select transfer modes
which ftp modes were implemented in rfc 412
subtitle: The Utah-10 FTP user's help file and command reference

tldr.problem: Users needed instructions for the Utah-10 FTP user process, whose help file was the only documentation then available.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC reproduces its command help, including editing keys, host selection, file operations and transfer settings.
tldr.outcome: Readers can see how the documented process was intended to manage and transfer files between hosts.

today: RFC 412 is the help documentation for a specific Utah-10 FTP user process, dated November 1972. It identifies which parts of that implementation were not yet available.

sections.title: The Utah-10 FTP User Process
sections.content: The document is the help file displayed by the Utah-10 User FTP Process when a user types HELP. The author says it was the only documentation produced to that point. The process was designed to make transfers between ARPANET hosts easier through a command language intended to be natural to use.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC is the help screen for Utah-10's FTP program. It serves as a command guide for transferring files between hosts.

sections.title: Commands for Selecting Hosts and Files
sections.content:
Users could select a host by name or number, then use commands such as RETRIEVE or GET to receive a remote file and STORE or SEND to send a local file. Other commands append, rename or delete remote files, list file groups, check status, log in and end a session.

The help text describes COPY for groups of local or remote files and shows an example session that connects to more than one host.
sections.plainLanguage: The command list covers choosing a host, logging in, sending or receiving files, and managing remote file names. COPY can work with groups of files.

sections.title: Transfer Mode and Data Type
sections.content:
The MODE command selects a transfer mode. The help text lists STREAM, BLOCK, TEXT and HASP, but states that only STREAM and TEXT were implemented at the time. BYTE sets the data connection's byte size, while TYPE chooses a data representation such as TENEX, ASCII, IMAGE or LOCAL.

The help text also describes a STRUCTURE command for indicating whether the data stream carries record structure information.
sections.plainLanguage: Users could choose how the data moved and how it was represented. The document notes that only STREAM and TEXT modes were implemented then.

sections.title: Help, Editing and a Sample Session
sections.content:
The command interpreter can list available commands when the user types a question mark. Control characters let users edit or abort command input, and the help text explains how passwords are entered without being echoed. A sample session shows login, retrieval, storage and session closure.

The document also marks some commands or data types as not yet implemented, including SOCKET and several TYPE options.
sections.plainLanguage: The help command can show available commands, and control characters can edit or cancel input. The sample session illustrates file transfers, while the notes identify features not yet implemented.
